units.translation: What mortal man will escape the god's deceitful trickery?
from which it is not possible for a mortal to escape and flee.
I say that your head will not escape justice — the curses of stoning.
It is a Homeric word, which the grammarians cited in the Thesaurus vol. 1 p. 1602 explain by εὑρετικός [inventive], συνετός [intelligent], ἐπινοητικός [resourceful].
the prosperity of inventive men, grown too fat
a great circle, I mean the circle of the shield
a paean celebrating the capture of the city
the message of the captured city
having raised the paean of capture with a wild cry
announcing the capture and destruction of Troy
by all means ward off the capture by enemies

I restored the apocope at Suppl. 782, where in M is read: τὸ πᾶν δ᾽ ἄφαντος ἀμπετήσαις δόσως | κόνις ἄτερθεν πτερύγων ὀλοίμαν [and I, wholly invisible, having flown up with gifts, may I perish as dust without wings]. The monstrosities of words ἀμπετήσαισδόσως [having flown up with gifts], like not a few others in the last part of this play, owe their origin to an older manuscript, in which some letters could scarcely be read, others had completely vanished. I therefore restored what the sense requires: ἃμ πνοαῖς διψάς ὡς [as thirsty dust with the breezes]. ἅμ [with] is used for ἅμα [at the same time] (much as ἄμ [up] is used for ἀνά [up]) in a gloss of Hesychius, although not much weight should be given to him. ἅμα πνοαῖς [with the breezes] is said as in Homer Il. 15, 149 ἅμα πνοιῇσι πετέσθην [they flew with the breezes], and with the addition of ἀνέμοιο [of the wind] Od. 2, 148 ἐπέτοντο μετὰ πνοιῇς ἀνέμοιο [they flew amid the breezes of the wind]. διψάς κόνις [thirsty dust] is to be compared with διψία κόνις [thirsty dust], which Aeschylus Agam. 495 and Sophocles Antig. 246, 429 used.
at the same time as this
speaking of a foreign and a civic pollution at once, a double defilement that appeared before the city
AG. Thus they were slain too much by kindred hands. CH. Thus the divine power was common to both at once.
and at the same time raised a shrill cry
dishonoring your husband's bed, did you at the same time plot this death for your husband the general?
the breast, at which you often slumbering at the same time drew out nourishing milk with your gums
and I, wholly invisible, having flown up with gifts, may I perish as dust without wings
as thirsty dust with the breezes
they flew amid the breezes of the wind
by a woman, not with impetuous far-shooting bows, like an Amazon
there you will come upon the man-hating army of the Amazons
and destroys him who speaks loudly with hostile anger
